netMetering: kWh you export are credited by the supplier: as money at the selling price and/or as a kWh credit that reduces future purchases. Turn it on if your contract buys your surplus.
sellRatio: Share of the buying price paid for an exported kWh when the zone has no own selling price. 0.7 = 70 % of the buying price.
zoneRatio: Share of the kWh exported in this zone that become a credit against future purchases. 1 = every exported kWh cancels one bought.
defaultZone: Applies in hours and days no zone takes. Without one, energy in such hours is not priced.
zoneDays: The zone applies only on the ticked days. Where zones overlap the hub picks the more important one: peak over day, weekend over weekdays.
role: What the sensor measures: the input (the whole house from the grid), solar or another source, a single load. The role drives the flow diagram, money and advice.
phase: Which input phase this sensor's line is on. It sets the reference voltage and how the line's load is split across the input's phases.
partial: The hub did not record the whole hour or day — it was off or restarting. The value is right for the time it ran.
notBought: Solar energy the house used itself. It did not have to be bought — valued at the period's average buying price.
closedRecords: The hub writes the totals of each hour, day and month after it ends. The running hour is added when it ends; the Overview already counts it from the live counters.
